carla_support: :rotating_light: Support escalated — multiple customers reporting p95/p99 API latency spikes (text-generation) in ap-south-1 since ~09:12 UTC, started ~2h ago. Some 504s seen. Ticket #CS-4219.
ben_sre: copying graphs now — I see p95 from 180ms -> 1.6s, p99 to ~4.2s on replicas in ap-south-1. Any infra changes in the window?
mira_prod: we started a targeted CUDA driver rollout to ap-south yesterday, gradual. last batch finished ~07:30 UTC.
dave_eng_infra: yup, driver 555.2 -> 556.0 landed on GPU hosts this morning. noticable nvme qdepth bumps on a subset of nodes.
carla_support: customers reporting auth/timeouts while calling generate endpoint. payloads normal. We have a repro trace from customer A with request-id: req-0a1b2c3d.
ben_sre: can you paste the failing request logs? I want the full latency trace (gateway -> backend -> model).
carla_support: pasted below: 
```
[09:14:02] gateway recv req-0a1b2c3d
[09:14:02] proxy -> frontend auth ok (20ms)
[09:14:03] frontend -> runtime enqueue (120ms)
[09:14:04] runtime wait qdepth (1.1s)
[09:14:06] runtime -> gpu-host dispatch (200ms)
[09:14:10] gpu-host stall -> 504
```
ben_sre: runtime wait qdepth is the red flag. can we get iostat / nvme top for affected nodes?
dave_eng_infra: pulling outputs now. snippet from node gpu-aps-12: 
```
$ iostat -x 1 3
Device            r/s     w/s   r_await  w_await  aqu-sz  %util
nvme0n1         123.4  987.6   0.82     9.21    12.8   98.4
```
ben_sre: %util ~98 and aqu-sz high -> starvation. Also hit dmesg entries of nvme queue full/timeouts?
dave_eng_infra: yes: 
```
[09:10:55] nvme nvme0: I/O 0x7f8a timed out
[09:11:03] nvme nvme0: controller reset
```
mira_prod: hm, driver 556 changed NVME queue handling and submitted a new default IO scheduler for our distro. possible regression in driver/kernel interaction.
ben_sre: do we have nodes still on 555.2 to compare?
dave_eng_infra: ~30% of ap-south fleet still on 555.2. comparing metrics: older nodes show p95 ~210ms, new nodes at 1.5s. definite correlation.
carla_support: customers asking for ETA on fix — any short-term mitigations?
dave_eng_infra: mitigation options: 1) rollback driver on affected pool (fast, but needs node reboot), 2) temporarily throttle background writer tasks to reduce NVMe pressure (safe), 3) route traffic away from impacted nodes via graceful draining.
ben_sre: let's do quickest: throttle background writers + cordon/drain hottest nodes into standby. Start rolling rollback after we confirm stability.
carla_support: will update customers.
dave_eng_infra: commands we'll run: 
```
# throttle writer (systemd service)
systemctl stop bulk-writer.service
# cordon + drain node
kubectl cordon gpu-aps-12 && kubectl drain gpu-aps-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
```
ben_sre: also enabling KV-cache prefix reuse to reduce IO bursts for large batched requests — config change pushed to runtime: 
```
runtime.config.kv_cache.use_prefix_reuse=true
```
mira_prod: starting throttle now on 6 nodes. monitoring.
infra-bot: Deploy event: throttle-bulk-writer started by dave_eng_infra at 09:38 UTC.
dave_eng_infra: after stopping writers on the 6 nodes, avg aqu-sz fell from 12.8 -> 2.1 and p95 dropped to ~240ms. p99 down to ~650ms.
ben_sre: good. proceed to cordon+drain 4 hottest nodes and failover pods. I'll watch for new 504s.
dave_eng_infra: draining node gpu-aps-12 now. planning rollback can wait until end of current ticket window; prefer targeted rollback if throttle+drain does full recovery.
carla_support: customers updated: "partial mitigation in place, investigating root cause, may require short reboots for full fix" — they responded :thumbsup:.
ben_sre: postmortem action items: - bisect driver kernel interactions with nvme-cli fio workload - add IO qdepth alert earlier (aqu-sz > 4) - provide rollback runbook for driver rollouts - add graceful traffic shift knob to routing policy.
mira_prod: noted. will pause further driver rollouts to other regions until root cause found.
dave_eng_infra: saving logs and fio reproducer, sharing link: https://internal.redwood/ops/CS-4219/repro-logs.
carla_support: closing the customer escalation for now (customers acknowledged mitigation). leaving incident open for follow-up actions.
ben_sre: great job triage team. :trophy:
carla_support: adding post-incident blameless notes and owner assignment to infra for bisect (dave_eng_infra).
ben_sre: last note — if rollback needed, prefer targeted kernel/driver combo rollback to 555.2 with staged reboots. Avoid full fleet simultaneous reboots.
carla_support: ack. thanks everyone!
